hints: The row and column motions are independent reflections.
Unfold each reflection into straight-line motion and fold its coordinate back.
Direction changes occur at multiples of n-1 or m-1, counting simultaneous hits once.
analogy: Imagine reflecting the board at every border so the ball always travels straight in the unfolded plane.
example: On a 3 by 4 board after 3 steps, the ball is at (2,4) and has changed direction twice.
algorithm: Let H=n-1 and W=m-1. For either dimension with extent L, set z=k mod (2L), and its one-based coordinate is 1+min(z,2L-z). Count direction changes as floor(k/H)+floor(k/W)-floor(k/lcm(H,W)), where a corner hit changes direction only once. Compute lcm with gcd and sufficiently wide integer arithmetic.
correctness: In the unfolded plane each coordinate increases by one per step; folding a period of 2L gives its reflected position. Hits on horizontal and vertical borders occur at positive multiples of H and W respectively. Inclusion-exclusion counts their union, including a hit exactly at step k and counting corner hits once.
complexity: Each test takes O(log(min(n,m))) time for gcd and O(1) space.
